description:
Managed UAT now uses an engine-resolved compose CLI: BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI overrides the choice, and on macOS mocker is selected when present before docker. Native Apple container tooling is used for container-store cleanup. This TODO is therefore not a migration task; it closes the remaining gap between the engine-agnostic implementation and release-grade managed-stack evidence.\n\nThe historical 2026-05-28 evidence remains unusable: the managed non-OLTP cells.jsonl was empty after a LakeSail startup timeout, and the managed OLTP run root was empty. Revalidate under the resolved managed engine, using Mocker on the current macOS path, into a fresh run root. Measure a healthy LakeSail compose-up before changing cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s, preserve the failure-capture-and-advance behavior, and run the managed tiers only in the release-gate order after native and dataframe stages. Each stack remains serialized and must produce up, run, and down lifecycle records plus non-empty result artifacts.\n\nMocker coverage is partial: QuestDB and PostgreSQL lifecycle parity plus QuestDB end-to-end execution are validated; Databend’s separate MinIO dependency has a known Mocker failure, while Doris and StarRocks still need separate Mocker validation. Use BENCHBOX_CONTAINER_CLI=docker only for a stack with a documented Mocker incompatibility, and record the exception and evidence. Do not treat unit tests as full Mocker coverage.\n\nUnblock by confirming Apple container and Mocker storage and memory headroom, measuring healthy LakeSail startup, setting cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s above that measurement with evidence, then running the managed smoke and release-gate rerun into a fresh root.

REVALIDATED 2026-08-23: under Mocker 0.7.2 / Apple Container 1.1.0, isolated LakeSail startup completed successfully in 5 seconds. After a 15-second post-start wait, `mocker compose ps -a` reported lakesail-connect `Up` on port 50051; teardown completed successfully. Evidence: /tmp/benchbox-lakesail-startup-20260823.log and /tmp/benchbox-lakesail-poststart-20260823.log. The 2026-08-17 memory-shortfall blocker is stale for this stack startup path. A full release-gate rerun and other managed stacks remain separate evidence requirements.

REVALIDATED 2026-08-23 managed smoke: LakeSail startup/readiness passed and teardown succeeded, but the fresh-root smoke aborted before ClickHouse execution at the host-memory gate. On source d224a6932, clickhouse-server requested 7.451 GiB plus the 2.00 GiB reserve; only 5.34 GiB was available with 70.2% swap, so the required 9.45 GiB threshold failed. Evidence: /Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_docker_managed_20260823/uat_lifecycle.log and matrix_summary.partial.tsv. This supersedes the old LakeSail-startup blocker; rerun after the 5.25 GiB ClickHouse policy PR is integrated and/or on a host with measured headroom.

REVALIDATED 2026-08-23 after PR #1835 merged as 4f8c580f7: managed smoke resolves clickhouse_memory_limit=5.25g. LakeSail startup/readiness and teardown pass; the run then aborts before ClickHouse startup at the current host-memory gate: 5.40 GiB available versus 6.89 GiB required (5.25 GiB request plus 2.00 GiB reserve), with 67.9% swap. Evidence: /Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_docker_managed_20260823/uat_lifecycle.log and matrix_summary.partial.tsv.

RECONCILED 2026-08-24: the calibration established the 5.25 GiB ClickHouse runtime request but did not validate the additional 2 GiB host reserve. Follow-up PR #1867 removes that unvalidated default, retains explicit nonzero overrides, and adds regression coverage. The prior 6.89 GiB admission blocker must not be treated as a measured requirement; rerun the merged request-only policy after #1867 lands.

PRE-MERGE REQUEST-ONLY RUN 2026-08-24 on PR #1867 head e70f2ff59: ClickHouse compose up succeeded and runtime stats matched the 5.25g request exactly with reserve=0.00 GiB. Post-start available memory fell to 4.78 GiB versus 4.889 GiB required, with 76.5% swap, so readiness failed closed; LakeSail also started/teardown-cleanly, while CedarDB/StarRocks had separate startup failures. Evidence: /Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_docker_managed_20260824/uat_lifecycle.log and matrix_summary.tsv. This confirms the old 2 GiB reserve was not the ClickHouse requirement; remaining failure is genuine current-host pressure below the measured request.

MERGED-STATE RUN 2026-08-24 on develop 466dd64c8 after PR #1867 merge 5479a967: LakeSail compose up and teardown succeeded, but its cell failed because generated UAT argv injected `--platform-option endpoint=sc://localhost:50051` and current CLI rejected endpoint for lakesail (only driver_auto_install/driver_version advertised). ClickHouse then reached request-only runtime admission with 5.25g/0.00 GiB reserve but failed closed at 4.73 GiB available < 4.889 GiB required, swap 64.0%. Evidence: /Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_docker_managed_20260824/uat_lifecycle.log and lakesail_tpch_0.01_20260824_132920.log.

FOLLOW-UP FIX 2026-08-24: PR #1875 (60e4363cb) registers the `endpoint` platform option for LakeSail and Velox, matching managed UAT Spark Connect endpoint injection. Focused tests: 152 passed; preflight passed. Await merge before the next authoritative managed run.

anti_patterns.dont: let one compose-up timeout abort the entire Docker sweep.
raise docker_start_timeout_s until you have measured a healthy startup
anti_patterns.why: a longer timeout on a broken service just wastes 5+ minutes per attempt.

anti_patterns.dont: reuse the empty 2026-05-28 oltp run dir as evidence
anti_patterns.why: it has none; re-run into a fresh root.

work_units.notes:
Mechanism + guidance delivered (CODE part). docs/operations/uat-framework.md
now documents the measure-then-set procedure: bring the stack up in
isolation (make uat-bring-up PLATFORM=lakesail), confirm health, time it,
then set cleanup.docker_start_timeout_s above the observed healthy time.
Per the anti-pattern the global default is NOT raised blindly. The actual
LakeSail value must be set from a measured healthy startup during the
release-gate bring-up (requires building the benchbox-lakesail Spark
Connect image, which is the live-environment step folded into the
release-gate re-run; see uat-certification-rerun-ordering-and-gate w5).

work_units.evidence: tests/uat/phases/execute.py records managed compose-up failures as skipped-unreachable, tears down the half-started stack, and advances; focused Docker/UAT suite: 186 passed.
work_units.notes:
Fixed in tests/uat/phases/execute.py: a managed compose-up failure
(cleanup_status == "startup-failed") now records the platform's cells as
skipped-unreachable (the failure is captured in docker_events /
uat_lifecycle.log action=up status=failed), tears down the half-started
stack, and advances to the next stack — instead of breaking the whole
sweep. Genuine global aborts (free space, teardown failure, fixed
container-name policy) still abort. Regression test:
tests/uat/test_phases.py::test_execute_docker_startup_failure_records_and_advances_to_next_platform.
NOTE: this required editing tests/uat/phases/execute.py + test_phases.py,
which were outside the original scope_limit only_modify list (the FAIL-
and-advance machinery was assumed owned by uat-artifact-integrity-and-
failure-capture #691, but #691 did not make compose-up failure non-fatal).
scope_limit expanded below with this justification.

work_units.notes:
OPERATIONAL / live-environment step. NOT independently actionable and NOT
a standalone Docker-only rerun: it is executed ONLY inside the four-stage
release-gate sweep [[uat-certification-rerun-ordering-and-gate]] w5
(native -> dataframe -> docker non-OLTP -> docker OLTP), which runs the
Docker OLTP stacks into a fresh root rather than running the re-run twice.
Running just the Docker stacks here would reproduce the ordering
contamination that w5's anti-pattern forbids ("DO NOT start a Docker stack
before native + dataframe platforms finish"). Kept `status: pending`
(the schema allows only pending/in_progress/done) but the summary and these
notes mark it as cert-w5-owned so the ready queue is not mistaken for a
standalone task. Requires built/pulled Docker images (OLTP stacks) + the
live Docker daemon. The empty 2026-05-28 oltp dir is non-evidentiary.
